title: Characterising Global Platforms: Centralised, Decentralised, Federated, and Grassroots
abstract: arXiv:2511.03286v5 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Global digital platforms are distributed systems designed to serve entire populations, with some already serving billions of people. Here we propose atomic transactions-based multiagent transition systems and protocols as a formal framework to study them; introduce essential agents---minimal sets of agents the removal of which makes communication impossible; and show that the cardinality of essential agents partitions all global platforms into four classes:   1. Centralised (Facebook) -- one (the server)   2. Decentralised (Bitcoin) -- finite >1 (bootstrap nodes)   3. Federated (Mastodon) -- infinite but not universal (all servers)   4. Grassroots (Scuttlebutt) -- universal (all agents but one)   Our illustrative formal example is a global social network, for which we provide centralised, decentralised, federated, and grassroots specifications via multiagent atomic transactions, and prove they all satisfy the same basic correct

translated_title: 刻画全球平台：中心化、去中心化、联邦化与草根化
translated_abstract: 全球数字平台是为服务整个人群而设计的分布式系统，其中一些平台已经服务于数十亿用户。本文提出基于原子事务的多智能体转换系统与协议作为研究此类平台的形式化框架；引入“必要智能体”的概念——即移除后将导致通信无法进行的智能体最小集合；并证明必要智能体的基数可将所有全球平台划分为四类：1. 中心化（如Facebook）——仅一个（服务器）；2. 去中心化（如比特币）——有限多个且大于1（引导节点）；3. 联邦化（如Mastodon）——无限多个但非普遍（所有服务器）；4. 草根化（如Scuttlebutt）——普遍存在（除一个之外的所有智能体）。我们的示例性形式化案例是一个全球社交网络，我们通过多智能体原子事务为其提供了中心化、去中心化、联邦化和草根化四种规范，并证明它们均满足相同的基本正确性。
tldr: 本文提出基于原子事务的多智能体转换系统这一形式化框架，通过“必要智能体”的基数将全球数字平台划分为中心化、去中心化、联邦化和草根化四个类别。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a formal framework based on atomic transactions-based multiagent transition systems, which partitions all global digital platforms into four classes—centralised, decentralised, federated, and grassroots—according to the cardinality of essential agents.
